lines.en: I wake up again. A terrible start to the day.
Hello, world.
No reply. As expected.
I grab a half-emptied water bottle from the nightstand and pour its contents down my throat.
Millions of bacterial organisms that snuck into the bottle overnight are consumed in the process.
Goodbye, new friends.
Please enjoy the warm embrace of my intestines.
And please thank them on your way down as I have lost the motivation required to do it myself.
Ami doesn’t make me breakfast anymore.

There’s no sweet-smelling aroma sneaking in through the crack underneath my door, and there’s no light that finds its way into the room as I’ve been pulling the curtains closed a little bit tighter than I used to.
Every once in a while, I have to clean things up around here.
I’m not very good at it yet. I’m not even sure where Ami keeps most of the supplies.

I don’t know the right way to remove stains from the carpet or which cleaning fluid is best used on the bathroom tiles. And if it weren’t for expiration dates, I’d probably be eating rotten food as well.
It’s fine, though.
Ami manages to bathe without the help of a sponge, so she’s already better than I was in that regard.
But she has a hard time looking at me now.
She feels guilty.
She keeps looking at my hand in the very short bursts of time in which she’s not zoned out and staring at the ceiling.
It’s fine, though.
I’m sure she just needs some time. So I’ll keep doing my best to get stains out of the carpet and soap residue off of the bathroom tiles while taking careful note of all the expiration dates.
Ami doesn’t ever smile anymore.
It’s fine, though.
She just takes after me.
I glance over at my phone to see a call from an unknown number.
Which is exactly why I decide to answer it.
: Hello?
: Uhh...hey.
: ...Osako?
: Yeah. S...Surprise!
: Did...something happen? You never call me. I didn’t even know you had my number.
: Yeah. I kind of stole it out of Wakana’s phone while she was in the shower this morning.
: To...check in on you, I guess. I haven’t seen you in months. But I heard from Wakana you actually showed up to school the other day?
: Yeah. Just long enough to send everything spiraling into chaos, though.
: So, how long did that take? Five minutes?
: Give or take a few, yeah.
: Well, at least no one died. And things haven’t been all that exciting in the real world, so you can take some solace in that, I guess.
: Ayane’s been doing great in case you were wondering. She’s showing up at the dojo pretty regularly again.
: And, as expected, she’s a solid student when you’re not there to distract her.
: That’s good. But usually, when people call to “check in,” they try to avoid saying things that make the person they’re checking in on feel worse about themselves.
: Bullshit. We might not be all that close, but I know for sure something like that wouldn’t get to you. Especially when you already know it’s true.
: There are a lot of things I know to be true, but it doesn’t mean any of them make me feel good.
: Did your coma kill off the part of your brain that had a sense of humor? Do you want me to apologize?
: No. I’m just being an asshole because I’m not entirely sure how I’m supposed to talk to you after you stole my number out of your girlfriend’s phone.
: Does this mean you’re in love with me now?
: I don’t know. Do you have a vagina?
: Not that I’m aware of.
: Then it’s probably safe to assume I’m not in love with you.
: Why steal it, though? Why not just ask Wakana for my number if you really wanted to check in on me? I’m sure she wouldn’t mind.
: Because I don’t want her to know about this.
: Ahh...so you really are in love with me then.
: Yup. You got me. But confessing over the phone is so lame and, being the old-fashioned, heterosexual woman I am, I’d like to tell you how I really feel in person if that’s okay.
: You’re asking me to hang out? Behind Wakana’s back? As in, she can’t know about it?
: Yup.
: This isn’t about soup, is it? Because I’ve already been through that with her before and I was not able to help in any capacity.
: I can make my own fucking soup. Now, drag your sorry ass out of bed and come talk to me at the dojo.
: There’s no class today, so I can promise it’ll be just the two of us.
: That will come in handy considering all of the heterosexual sex we’re going to have together.
: Yeah. Can’t wait. Penis rules. When can you meet?
: Give me a couple hours. I have to make my niece breakfast and do a few things around the house.
: You know how to cook?
: No.
: Oh.
: Well, good luck then. Give me a call whenever you’re free. I don’t have anything going on today.
: Yeah...sounds good.
I hang up the phone and stare at the ceiling for a few more minutes, wondering what Osako could possibly want to see me for.
But I don’t wonder for long as I need to make sure Ami has everything she needs before I leave the house.
I make my way into her room and sit by her bedside for a moment.
She’s still asleep. That’s almost all she does now. But I find comfort in the fact that she might be happier when she’s dreaming as that’s how it always was for me.
I focus on her chest, watching her lungs expand and contract while thanking something out there that hers still function.
But as I get up off the floor and leave the room, I’m stricken with a depressing realization.
It’s the fact that I can leave at all.
It’s the fact that I don’t have to worry about anyone breaking in to save her when she had to deal with that on an almost constant basis.
I deserved rescue far less than she does.
I deserve nothing at all.
Yet I continue to reap the few benefits there are to existing while she gets spaghetti for the fifth day in a row because it’s all I’ve figured out how to cook.
It’s fine, though.
She looks cute with short hair.
I lock the door behind me and leave a note on the table that Ami probably won’t read.
But it’s there if she needs it.
Now, all that’s left to do is figure out why Osako wants to talk to me in person.
: HA!
I quickly discover that she just wants to kill me.
: Ngh!
: HAAAA!
: Keh!
: HAAAAAAAA!
: e
: Okay! I feel better now.
If I had known this was coming at the time of my departure, I would have noted something about my death in my letter to Ami.
Somewhat regretfully, I will die by the hand of a lesbian.
Or...foot, I guess would be more accurate.
Either way, it’s kind of beautiful that I, a man who has taken advantage of so many unassuming women, will be put out of my misery by a woman with no interest in men whatsoever.
Goodbye, world.
Again, no response.
: Oh, come on. Stop acting dead. If I wanted to kill you, I would have just done it.
: Go on then. Finish the job.
: Wow. You really are down in the dumps, aren’t you? You didn’t even try fighting back today.
: You’d think that might cause you to go a little easier on me...
: I’m glad you didn’t, though. I both deserve and needed this.
: Then why not stand back up and let me kick you some more? You’re actually pretty good as a punching bag.
: Sure. Just as soon as I regain control of my limbs.
: Wow. You might be even more of a masochist than me.
: It really does feel like that sometimes...
: Come on. I’ll help you up.
Osako rolls me onto my back and slaps my face a few times, which I don’t think is an official karate move, before grabbing my shoulders and pulling me upward.
She props me up using her hands for a few moments until I’m able to prevent myself from falling over.
Meanwhile, I begin to count down the minutes until I’m killed by cranial internal bleeding.
: What’s that look for? I basically just saved your life.
: Yeah, that’s why I’m mad.
: Oh? So it’s okay for me to kill you? I thought you were joking when you told me to finish the job.
: I both was and wasn’t. If you haven’t noticed, I’m kind of going through a lot of shit right now.
: Thanks for at least making me feel alive, though. I’ve been so numb to everything lately that this is, depressingly, the most fun I’ve had since October.
: And by “fun” I essentially just mean “something I don’t inherently despise.”
: Uhh...can I have my foot back?
: No. This is for my protection and yours.
: How does this protect me in literally any way whatsoever?
: It protects you from being jailed for manslaughter.
: You know what? Fair.
: Are you really that messed up, though? Because I get that...unexpected tragedy can put us out of commission for a while, but it’s been months, man. What’s going on?
: Well, first off, it’s only been months for you. I was unconscious for the vast majority of that time. And I wouldn’t have come here if I’d known you were going to make me talk about it.
: Okay. Then we won’t talk about it. I don’t need to know any of the specifics. But like, half the reason I called you here was to try and whip you back into shape.
: And the other half?
: ...Heterosexual sex?
: Hah...Wakana again?
: We’ll get to that later! Let’s talk about you now. But...in a way that doesn’t trigger your sudden interest in pain and death and stuff.
: Just go back to kicking me. There’s no way I can do that.
: Not with that attitude, there’s not. And maybe I’m jumping the gun here, but if you ever want to feel any better, moping around like this isn’t going to do you any good.
: Who says I want to feel better?
: Well...who in their right mind wants to feel like shit? What do you gain from that?
: I don’t know...retribution?
: Retribution? Are you some kind of character in one of Shakespeare’s plays all of a sudden?
: I guess Romeo and I do have our similarities.
: Listen, I’m not going to sit here and pretend that you’re a good guy when you do some very questionable things with your students on an almost routine basis.
: And you know...maybe you do deserve to be punished for that. Hell, I’ll be the first to admit that the reason I went so hard on you today was to get some of my own anger out.
: You don’t say.
: But it feels worse now that I know you wanted it. Like, punishment’s only punishment if the person being punished hates it. I get very little joy from putting you out of your misery.
: Then I’m sorry you did not adequately enjoy beating the shit out of me.
: Stop whining for a second and listen to me, man.
: How do you think everyone feels when they see you like this?
: They barely see me at all anymore.
: Then how do you think they feel knowing you’re like this?
: Warranted or not, there are a lot of people who really care about you. And I’m not saying you need to hurry up and “get over it” for all of their sakes as I know that’s straight up impossible.

: But feeling sorry for yourself all day every day is just going to make it even harder to get out of bed than it already is. And sooner or later, you’re even going to run out of shitty ways to internally insult yourself.
: Trust me on this. Feeling sorry for myself is probably my number one hobby after kicking stuff.
: But that’s where we’re different. You feel sorry for yourself because you’re insecure. I don’t feel sorry for myself at all. I hate myself. And pretending I don’t makes me feel even worse.
: So what am I supposed to do? Just act like everything’s okay so no one else worries while I continue to decay from the inside out? Mope around and try to stop it, just to make everyone else sick?
: Is being a better person just...not an option?
: I was trying.
: And just when I felt like I was finally starting to do better, I was punished for it.
: Now, the only thing that really mattered to me is gone and the only lesson I learned is to always do what I’m told or everything will fall apart.
: At least you’re free, Osako. And I’m here just struggling to comprehend how I’m supposed to feel human when I’m constantly reduced to a pawn in some...divine game of chess.
: Man, now I don’t even want to kick you. That’s depressing as hell.
: Tell me about it.
: Who was it that punished you, exactly? Your...niece? Yourself? What did that mean?
: Let’s just say it was a voice in the back of my head and call it a day.
: How are we gonna call it a day there? That’s like, the most vague bit of information you’ve given me so far.
: As long as you’re being honest about it, I mean. But why would you even lie to me in the first place?
: The thing is, it’s hard to say if I’m being honest at all. I don’t really know.
: Weird shit just...kind of happens to me sometimes. Chunks of the day disappear. My body acts on its own. I hear things. And some of the dreams I have are just...
: It’s hard.
: Do you want me to kick you again?
: I think that’d be great, actually.
: Then I think you’re going to have to release your grip on my foot.
: Will it immediately spring back up and knock me out? Or are we standing back up first? I just want to know when I should brace myself.
: We can stand back up first.
: Fine. Then-
: Ngh!
: Oh, shit. That was harder than I thought it would be. Are you okay?
: More weight...
: Okay, maybe we should finish up for the day.
